author: Diptanu Choudhury
text: We are seeing backlash against sandboxes for primarily a couple of reasons - vendors don't support users to overcommit compute. You can't pay for N cores and overcommit the number of sandboxes that are run on those cores. In reality agents don't uniformly use resources during their lifecycle...
suggestedEngagement: Ask about what pricing/capacity models would solve the overcommit problem — e.g., spot-style billing vs reserved cores
Share perspective on how agent workload burstiness makes static compute allocation fundamentally broken for this use case
Challenge or affirm: is overcommit a vendor incentive problem (they want to sell more cores) or a technical risk-management problem?
